source.title: Cross-modal individual recognition in domestic horses (Equus caballus)
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: A clean expectancy-violation design in a non-primate showing that the representation of a specific individual is recoverable when the input crosses from the visual to the auditory subsystem -- close to the candidate's definition. Held below 0.8 because the boundary crossed is sensory rather than representational-geometric, and because the horse is a social mammal for whom conspecific identity is an ecological problem, so the embodied reading is not excluded.
failure_signatures: Modality-local familiarity would predict no response difference when a seen individual is followed by a different familiar individual's call; the observed violation response is the signature of a cross-modal identity representation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Horses responded faster, looked longer and looked more often when a familiar herd member walked past out of sight and was then followed by a different familiar individual's whinny than when the call matched, indicating a multi-modal representation of a specific individual.
mapping.ree_translation: The IDENTITY relation survives translation between two sensory subsystems in a non-primate. GOV-CONTRACT-1 domain 4 asks whether a distinction appears in species with different ecologies; together with mirror self-recognition in magpies (Prior et al. 2008) and the contested cleaner-wrasse result (Kohda et al. 2019), the identity relation recurs across mammal, bird and teleost lineages.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Sensory cross-modality is an easier boundary than the inter-engine boundary ARC-142 names; and every species with positive evidence is social, so the relation may be recurrent because individual recognition is a shared ecological problem rather than because unified cognition requires it.
mapping.source_context: Domestic horses, naturalistic cross-modal expectancy-violation playback design.
